interpretation_notes: Each boundary marker separates two proposed word-like or meaningful units.
Read a marked string such as Donne¦-¦le¦-¦moi as the proposed units Donne, -, le, -, moi.
Spaces, hyphens, apostrophes, and punctuation can be separate units; do not reject an example merely because these separators have been split out.
Deterministic validation has already checked that removing the boundary markers recreates the input exactly.

review.explanation: The split treats l’ as the elided definite article, and separates the negative markers ne and pas from the verb, all of which are learner-relevant clitic/functional pieces. Handling of the apostrophe with the article is acceptable under the guidance, and the remaining units are standard words/punctuation.
notes: Makes the ne … pas negation visible as two units around the verb.
Elided article l’ shown as a reusable piece before a vowel-initial noun.
Keeping spaces/punctuation as separate units is allowed and not misleading here.
